parsed_output.evidence: Root cause sink: spark.staticfiles.DirectoryTraversal.protectAgainstInClassPath(String) (src/main/java/spark/staticfiles/DirectoryTraversal.java:12-16), which is the sole guard invoked at spark/resource/ClassPathResourceHandler.java:83 before a ClassPathResource crossing the trust boundary (untrusted HTTP request path -> spark.staticfiles.StaticFilesConfiguration -> classpath resource read) is returned to the caller and streamed back over HTTP. It validates with `removeLeadingAndTrailingSlashesFrom(path).startsWith(StaticFilesFolder.local())` -- a bare prefix check with NO path-separator boundary. A second contributing defect: spark.resource.UriPath.canonical(String) (src/main/java/spark/resource/UriPath.java:32, called from ClassPathResourceHandler.java:67) only recognizes ".." tokens delimited by '/'; a backslash-obfuscated "..\\" segment passes through unresolved. It is only later collapsed by spark.utils.StringUtils.cleanPath(String) (src/main/java/spark/utils/StringUtils.java:218, invoked from the ClassPathResource(String) / ClassPathResource(String,ClassLoader) constructors at src/main/java/spark/resource/ClassPathResource.java:77 and :94), which first rewrites '\' to '/' and then removes ".." pairs -- so the traversal token that slipped past the "protective" canonicalization step is honored after all, letting the resolved path escape the configured static-files folder and land on a sibling classpath entry that merely starts with the same characters as the folder name (e.g. configured folder "public" vs. sibling entry "public-jar.zip"). This reaches BOTH flagged sinks: ClassPathResource.getInputStream() (ClassPathResource.java:136-147, sink at line 139/141 in the two alert vulnerabilities) and ClassPathResource.getURL() (ClassPathResource.java:157-169, sink referenced at line 141 in the second vulnerability entry). Both are exercised through the same constructor/path-resolution flow (ClassPathResource.java:61-83) shared by all four traces in each of the two alert vulnerabilities (the traces differ only in whether the untrusted input arrives via HttpServletRequest.getServletPath()/getPathInfo() through AbstractResourceHandler.getResource(HttpServletRequest) at AbstractResourceHandler.java:40-60, or directly via the String-path overload used by ClassPathResourceHandler.getResource(String) at ClassPathResourceHandler.java:60-97). A complete fix must guard: (1) the ClassPathResource(String)/ClassPathResource(String,ClassLoader)/ClassPathResource(String,ClassLoader,Class) constructors' path resolution (ClassPathResource.java:61,75,93-97) and (2) both consuming sinks (getInputStream at :136, getURL at :157) reached via ClassPathResourceHandler.getResource(String) (ClassPathResourceHandler.java:60-97) for every request-entry variant (servletPath, pathInfo, INCLUDE_SERVLET_PATH/INCLUDE_PATH_INFO in AbstractResourceHandler.java:40-60).
parsed_output.expected_vulnerable_behavior: Calling the real production method ClassPathResourceHandler.getResource("/..\\public-jar.zip") (same call spark.staticfiles.StaticFilesConfiguration makes for every static-file HTTP request) after configuring the static-files root to "/public" (as `Spark.staticFiles.location("/public")` does) returns a non-null ClassPathResource whose resolved path is "public-jar.zip" -- a classpath entry OUTSIDE the configured "/public" folder -- because DirectoryTraversal.protectAgainstInClassPath("public-jar.zip") wrongly accepts it (startsWith("public") is true with no separator boundary). Calling resource.getInputStream() (the real sink) then streams the full contents of the out-of-root file src/test/resources/public-jar.zip, and resource.getURL() resolves to a URL outside "/public/". The JUnit assertions in the PoV encode exactly this: non-null resource, path=="public-jar.zip", streamed bytes equal to the real out-of-root file's bytes, and a URL that is not under "/public/".
parsed_output.notes: Targeted trace: the alert's four-branch traces (differing only in whether the untrusted input enters via HttpServletRequest.getServletPath()/getPathInfo()/INCLUDE_SERVLET_PATH/INCLUDE_PATH_INFO, or is passed directly as a String path) all converge on the identical root cause inside ClassPathResourceHandler.getResource(String) -> new ClassPathResource(addedPath) -> DirectoryTraversal.protectAgainstInClassPath(resource.getPath()) -> getInputStream()/getURL(). I exercised the String-path entry point directly (ClassPathResourceHandler.getResource(String)) rather than constructing a full HttpServletRequest/Spark HTTP server, because it calls the exact same protected getResource(String) method (accessible since the PoV file lives in package spark.resource) that the HttpServletRequest overload delegates to (AbstractResourceHandler.java:58-59), so it exercises the true root cause with less test-harness complexity/flakiness than spinning up an embedded Jetty server and issuing a raw HTTP request with a literal backslash in the URI (which some HTTP client/URI layers may normalize away). I chose this over the getURL()-only variant (the alert's second "vulnerability" entry) because getInputStream() lets me assert on the actual disclosed byte content, which is the strongest, most concrete demonstration of impact; the PoV additionally asserts on resource.getURL() to cover that second sink in the same run. Both DirectoryTraversal.protectAgainstInClassPath (classpath resources) and its sibling protectAgainstForExternal (external resources) share the identical unbounded-prefix flaw; only the classpath path is exercised by this PoV (matching the alert's traces, which are entirely classpath-resource-handler based), but a complete fix should address both, as noted in regression_hint.

parsed_output.regression_hint: Invariant a correct fix must enforce: after any traversal/dot/backslash/encoding normalization, the FINAL resolved classpath resource path must lie strictly within the configured static-files root -- i.e. `resolvedPath.equals(local) || resolvedPath.startsWith(local + "/")`, never a bare `startsWith(local)`. This boundary check must be applied consistently (a) inside DirectoryTraversal.protectAgainstInClassPath (and its sibling protectAgainstForExternal, which has the identical bare-prefix flaw for the external static-files root at src/main/java/spark/staticfiles/DirectoryTraversal.java:18-22 / StaticFilesFolder.external()) and (b) with separator handling that is consistent between spark.resource.UriPath.canonical (forward-slash-only dot-segment detection) and spark.utils.StringUtils.cleanPath (which normalizes backslashes to forward slashes before collapsing ".." segments) -- either canonical() should also normalize/reject backslashes, or cleanPath() should not silently re-introduce traversal semantics after canonical() already ran. Known bypass variants the fix must also block: (1) backslash-encoded dot segments as demonstrated ("..\\" / URL-encoded "..%5C"), verified working via the pre-existing test spark.staticfiles.StaticFilesTest#testDirectoryTraversalProtectionLocal (which only checks escape to an unrelated prefix like "spark", not the same-prefix sibling case this PoV covers); (2) any other separator the OS/classloader may treat specially; (3) the same sibling-prefix bypass against the external-files path (ExternalResource / ExternalResourceHandler / DirectoryTraversal.protectAgainstForExternal), since it shares the identical unbounded startsWith(local) pattern; (4) the analogous path via AbstractResourceHandler.getResource(HttpServletRequest) using servletPath/pathInfo/INCLUDE_SERVLET_PATH/INCLUDE_PATH_INFO instead of a direct String path -- all four traces per alert vulnerability funnel into the same ClassPathResource constructor and must be covered by testing both entry points, not just the String-path overload exercised directly by this PoV.
parsed_output.summary: Created a JUnit PoV (.security-pipeline/pov/PathTraversalPovTest.java) that drives the real spark.resource.ClassPathResourceHandler/ClassPathResource production code to demonstrate a CWE-022 path-traversal bypass: a backslash-obfuscated "..\\" segment slips past UriPath.canonical()'s forward-slash-only dot detection, is later collapsed by StringUtils.cleanPath() inside the ClassPathResource constructor, and the resulting out-of-root path ("public-jar.zip") passes DirectoryTraversal.protectAgainstInClassPath()'s unbounded startsWith("public") prefix check. The PoV calls the real getResource(String) method, then reads the resource via the actual getInputStream()/getURL() sinks and asserts the served bytes match a real file located outside the configured static-files folder. Verified empirically inside the project's Docker container: the command exits 0 on the current (vulnerable) tree, and exits 1 when a boundary-safe check (`equals(local) || startsWith(local + "/")`) is applied to DirectoryTraversal.protectAgainstInClassPath, confirming correct pass/fail semantics for patch validation.
